question: cos(x - y) = frac{{sqrt 3 }}{2}, and sin(x + y) = 1, where x and y are positive acute angles and x ≥ y, then x and y are:
solution:
Given:

cos(x - y) = frac{{sqrt 3 }}{2} 

sin(x + y) = 1

**Concept used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3f554c2a905b798f1849a110ae992c5acc2a4505f5bdf6175494e44ee69e5b0.png] 

Calculation:

According to the concept used,

If cos(x - y) = frac{{sqrt 3 }}{2} 

⇒ x - y = 30°.....(1)

Again, sin(x + y) = 1

⇒ x + y = 90°....(2)

Now add 1 & 2

⇒ 2x = 120°

⇒ x = 60°

Similary, the value of y = 30°.

∴ The value of x and y is 60°, 30° respectively.
